Brief Hospital Course:

matures.

# ESRD:  Pt was admitted for tunnelled line placement and start 
of HD.  Line was placed on ___ and initial HD was on ___.  
Following placement, the pt experienced only mild discomfort at 
the site of the dialysis catheter insertion and this was 
controlled well with low dose oxycodone initially and was 
diminished significantly by discharge.  His hospital dietary 
regimen consisted of a diabetic, renal diet and the patient was 
given Nephro Caps.  In order to qualify for outpatient dialysis, 
the patient required a PPD, which was read on ___ as negative.  
Throughout admission the patient tolerated his dialysis sessions 
well and he was discharged on ___, with his first outpatient 
dialysis session scheduled for ___. 
.
# Insulin dependant diabetes mellitus:  Pt was continued on 
outpatient regimen of glucose control of NovoLog 70/30 and 
Actos.  An insulin sliding scale was ordered for additional 
coverage. Blood sugars were will controlled during admission and 
the pt was discharged without change in his home medications.
.
# Anemia:  Pt had a history of mild anemia which was 
significantly worse on admission.  This was presumed to reflect 
his worsening renal disease (AOCKD). Iron studies, b12, and 
folate were obtained and were normal.  Pt was started on Epogen 
at his dialysis sessions.
.
# Hyperlipidemia:  The patient was continued on his outpatient 
regimen of pravastatin and TriCor.  No changes were made during 
this admission.
.
# HTN:  Antihypertensives were held prior to HD. Upon 
discharged, the patient's pre-admission dose of doxazosin was 
decreased to 2mg daily.  No other changes were made.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for initiation of hemodialysis.  During this 
admission, you underwent placement of a tunneled hemodialysis 
catheter which was then used for your first few sessions of 
hemodialysis. Blood tests obtained following dialysis showed 
marked improvement in your fluid and electrolyte status.

You are being discharged with the hemodialysis catheter that was 
placed. This will be used for your future outpatient dialysis 
sessions while your permenant dialysis fistula matures. 

Because dialysis has affected your blood pressure by removing 
extra fluid, we have lowered your dose of blood pressure 
medications.  We recommend that you take your Cardura 
(Doxazosin) at a new dose of 2mg.  You will be given a 
prescription for this medication at discharge. Please take this, 
and any previously prescribed medications, as directed.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY: ___ year old man with diabetes and ESRD being admitted for HD
intiation.

PROCEDURE: Tunneled dialysis catheter placemnt.

RADIOLOGISTS:  The procedure was performed by Dr. ___ Dr. ___,
___ attending radiologist who was present and supervised the procedure.

COMPLICATIONS: None known.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Informed consent was obtained from the patient prior
to procedure after explaining risks and benefits of the procedure.  A
preprocedure timeout was performed documenting patient identity and the nature
of the procedure. Using ultrasound guidance, a micropuncture set
was used to gain access into the right internal jugular vein and a guide wire
was advanced into the distal SVC and the needle was removed. Hard copy
ultrasound images were obtained before and after venous access documenting
vessel patency. Incidentally noted, calcified plaque in the right carotid
artery. A 4.5 ___ vascular sheath was then advanced over the wire and the
wire was removed and replaced for ___ wire, which was advanced into the
right atrium. Appropriate measurements were taken for the dialysis line and
decision was made to use a 23-cm tip-to- cuff dialysis catheter. Attention was
then directed towards creation of subcutaneous tract.  Epinephrine buffered
lidocaine was instilled into the subcutaneous tissues for local anesthetic.
The dialysis catheter was the tunneled through the subcutaneous tissues and
exited near the right jugular vein puncture site. Sequential dilatation using
8, 12, and 14 ___ dilators then performed under fluoroscopic observation
over the ___ wire.  The 16 ___ peel-away sheath/inner dilator was then
advanced over the ___ wire under fluoroscopic observation into the SVC.  The
dilator and ___ wire were then removed and the hemodialysis catheter was
advanced through the peel-away sheath, which was subsequently removed.  A spot
fluoroscopic chest radiograph demonstrated appropriate positioning
hemodialysis catheter with its tip located within the right atrium.  The
dialysis catheter lumens were then flushed and heparin locked and the catheter
was secured using 0 silk sutures.   The patient tolerated the procedure well
with no immediate post- procedure complications. Total fluoroscopy time was
2.6 minutes.

MEDICATION: A total of 50 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed were given
during the 30 minutes total intraservice time.  The patient's hemodynamic
parameters were continuously monitored by nursing staff and remained stable.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of 23-cm tip-to-cuff tunneled dual-lumen
hemodialysis catheter via the right internal jugular vein. The distal tip is
located within the right atrium. The line is ready to use.
